passage_changes.passage: Climate change is reshaping the Arctic. Melting sea ice is opening new maritime corridors through waters that were once difficult to navigate. Shipping along these corridors could shorten travel times between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, while lowering fuel and shipping costs. The new routes could also allow ships to avoid some of the chokepoints that currently shape global trade. Control over these sea lanes is expected to influence future trade flows and the projection of naval power. Greenland's own resources add to the region's importance. The island holds mineral wealth that is vital for semiconductors, renewable energy equipment and defence systems. Many Western economies see new sources of these minerals as a way to diversify supply chains that are heavily concentrated elsewhere. This push forms part of a wider effort to decouple sensitive economic sectors from rival suppliers. China is also investing in Arctic research and infrastructure, which signals long-term interest in the region. Taken together, the changing Arctic is becoming a centre of economic and strategic competition, and the outcome will shape which countries gain leverage over future trade.

India's civilian honours include the Padma awards, which are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day. They recognise achievements in all fields involving public service and come in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri, listed in descending order of rank. The Bharat Ratna is described as India's highest civilian award. Gallantry awards recognise bravery shown by members of the armed forces, and they are kept in separate wartime and peacetime categories. Wartime Gallantry awards were instituted on 26 January 1950, while peacetime awards came later. Gallantry awards are announced twice a year, on Republic Day and Independence Day. Eligibility covers officers of all ranks in the Army, Navy and Air Force, reserve forces, the Territorial Army, and personnel providing nursing services under these forces. The order of precedence places the Param Vir Chakra first, followed by the Ashoka Chakra, Mahavir Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Vir Chakra and Shaurya Chakra. Gallantry awards are given for acts of bravery, while the Padma awards are given for service and achievement in public life. Each year the honours list covers a broad range of fields, and understanding the rank order of these awards helps in answering questions on both civilian and military honours.

The law of the sea rests on a simple idea: the closer a space lies to the coast, the greater a state's control over it. A state has full sovereignty over its territorial sea. Beyond that lies a zone in which the state holds the right to exploit all economic resources. Further still lie the high seas, where vessels of every nation may sail freely. The 1982 Convention on the Law of the Sea sets out the legal framework within which all activities in the oceans and seas must be carried out. It is often described as a constitution for the oceans. The Convention also created new institutions at the international level. One of these is a judicial body that settles disputes about how the Convention is interpreted. Another protects the marine environment from harmful effects of deep-seabed activities. A further body facilitates the establishment of the outer edge of the continental shelf. Continental shelf rights can extend beyond the basic zone limits, which makes the outer edge of the shelf a matter of legal importance. The Convention provides a process for determining that edge, and the bodies it created apply its rules in practice. The Convention is also supported by implementing agreements on particular issues, such as deep seabed mining and the management of fish stocks. Taken together, these rules form many layers of law that govern the oceans, and all users of the seas rely on this shared framework.

The National Sports Governance Act and its rules mark a major change in how sports are run in India. The key institutional mechanisms came into force in January 2026, after the Union Government notified the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026. The reforms aim to make sports administration more transparent, inclusive and accountable. At the centre of the system is an apex regulatory body that decides which national sports bodies remain recognised, and it keeps a central register of those bodies. Elections in sports federations will be overseen by a panel drawn from experienced former election officials, so that long-standing problems of conflict of interest and factionalism can be addressed. Disputes about athlete selection, elections and governance will go to a separate tribunal, which is meant to resolve cases independently, speedily and at a reasonable cost. Doping-related matters follow a different legal route. Every national sports body must also have a general body and an executive committee; the general body must include sportspersons and the executive committee must include women. The reforms are meant to curb politicisation, arbitrary decisions and the lack of accountability in sports administration. Beyond governance, the government runs programmes that encourage fitness, identify young talent and support athletes who aim to win medals at the Olympics.

Anti-doping rules in sport combine national law with international standards. A national agency under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports monitors doping control programmes across the country. India's standalone anti-doping law is designed to comply with the code of the World Anti-Doping Agency and gives authorities powers for search, seizure and disciplinary action. An international convention adopted by UNESCO urges nations to enact laws that eliminate drug use in sport, and it has been accepted by many countries, including India. When disagreements arise in the sports world, they can be taken to a specialised body that offers a fair and quick way to resolve them. Sport in India is also supported by government initiatives. The Fit India Movement encourages mass participation in fitness activities, while Khelo India identifies and develops athletes at grassroots and elite levels. The National Olympic Committee is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India. Recent results show the value of this support: Indian athletes won several medals at the Paris Olympics and Paralympics, and young players have also made headlines in chess and shooting. Talent identification programmes aimed at school children are meant to find promising players in every corner of India.

facts.title: Republic Day 2026 Parade and Chronology
facts.summary: Republic Day celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas, and conclude on 29 January with the Beating Retreat Ceremony at Vijay Chowk. The main events fall on 26 January, when the Prime Minister pays homage at the Amar Jawan Jyoti and the President unfurls the National Flag at Kartavya Path. The 2026 parade, the 77th Republic Day, showcased Constitutional values through 30 cultural tableaux.
facts: Festivities officially begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas.
23 January marks the birth anniversary of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose.
The President delivers the Republic Day Address on the day before Republic Day.
The Prime Minister pays homage at Amar Jawan Jyoti in early morning of 26 January.
The President unfurls the National Flag at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath).
The National Anthem and a 21-gun salute follow the flag unfurling and mark the formal start of the parade.
The President confers Padma and Gallantry Awards in the evening of 26 January.
Celebrations conclude on 29 January at Vijay Chowk with the Beating Retreat Ceremony.
2026 is India's 77th Republic Day; the theme is 150 Years of Vande Mataram.
Top tableaux: Maharashtra, Jammu & Kashmir and Kerala; Chief Guests: Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa.

facts.title: Rules 2026 and National Sports Bodies
facts.summary: The National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026 require every national sports body to have a General Body and an Executive Committee; the General Body must include sportspersons, and the Executive Committee at least 4 women. The National Olympic Committee and National Paralympic Committee are the sole governing bodies for Olympic and Paralympic sports in India. Recognised sports bodies are deemed public authorities under the RTI Act 2005.
facts: Rules 2026 require every National Sports Body to have a General Body and an Executive Committee
General Body must include at least 4 Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (minimum 25 years of age)
50% of Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit in the General Body must be women
Executive Committee must include at least 4 women members
National Olympic Committee is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India
National Paralympic Committee is the sole governing body for Paralympic sports
Other bodies include National Sports Federations and Regional Sports Federations
Term of members: 3 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
A person convicted by a court and sentenced to imprisonment is disqualified
Recognised sports bodies are deemed public authorities under the RTI Act 2005

facts.title: UN Security Council and Control Regimes
facts.summary: The UN Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations, established in 1945 under the UN Charter, and it has five permanent and ten non-permanent members. Its main purpose is maintaining international peace and security. Outside the Council, the Australia Group and the export control regimes NSG, MTCR and Wassenaar Arrangement work to limit the spread of dangerous weapons.
facts: UN Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the UN, established in 1945 under the UN Charter.
Permanent members (P5): China, France, Russia, USA and UK.
Ten non-permanent members; the General Assembly elects five each year for two-year terms.
Non-permanent seats are distributed on a regional basis.
UNSC presidency rotates every month among its 15 members.
UNSC headquarters: New York City; it authorises peacekeeping missions and imposes sanctions.
Coffee Club prime movers: Italy, Spain, Australia, Canada, South Korea, Argentina and Pakistan.
Coffee Club opposes expansion of permanent seats; Italy and Spain are opposed to Germany's bid, and Pakistan to India's bid.
Australia Group founded in 1985 after chemical weapons were used in the Iran-Iraq War; India joined in 2018.
NPT adopted 1968, in force 1970, extended indefinitely 1995; North Korea withdrew in 2003.
